newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Caracas stocks end up at third straight record.
newsitem.headline: Caracas stocks end up at third straight record.

text.p: Caracas stocks closed up to hit fresh highs for the third straight session in a row, propelled by continuing confidence in Venezuela's economic prospects, traders and analysts said.

"We continue to favor Mexico among the large markets and Venezuela among the smaller for new money," Morgan Stanley Dean Witter's Robert J. Pelosky said Monday in a Latin American equity research note.
The bolsa's 19-share index closed up 1.38 percent at 7,639.85 points as 126 million shares traded worth 7.5 billion bolivars ($15 million), according to preliminary data.
Merinvest's composite index, which includes telephone company CANTV, meanwhile rose 1.55 percent to end at 119.90 points.
"The bolsa's seen as a good long-term buy by foreign bidders," Financorp broker Miguel Ortiz said.

New York-based analysts IDEA agreed, and have targeted 8,300 points as the IBC index's next goal. But the group cautioned in a market comment that given the bolsa's steep 20 percent-plus rise since end-April, profit-taking was likely.
"We suggest traders look for a setback before adding to positions. Suggested buy level is 7345/7300 (points)."
Food company Mavesa led gainers, rising 7.11 percent to end at 113.00 bolivars.
Among traded stocks, 29 rose, ten fell and six closed flat.
